# Pre-registration (approved by the user 2026-09-24; frozen with the campaign)

execution_plan §15: "Pre-register final metric definitions, the freeze commits, exclusion rules, and analysis scripts
before the final campaign." The user approved the proposals below on 2026-09-24 (the alternatives are kept for the
record). Every run records its full raw data (docs/preflight_checklist.md R1), so these are computed from it at
analysis time; a later change of definition is recomputed, never re-simulated.

## 1. `preplanned_transition_fraction` (ALFUS "portion of the mission pre-generated by humans", §14.2)

Problem with the draft in `evaluation/rows.py` (label every executed call human_preauthored / planner_generated /
agent_generated_online): it is a property of the method, not of the run -- PLEXIL 1.0, EUROPA 1.0 (the solver only
instantiates decomposition knowledge a human wrote into the domain), Ours 0.0 in every run. A column that is constant
per method says nothing a reader does not already know.

**Decided:** per instance, from its closed-capability certificate (the valid solution sequence), the fraction of that
solution's transitions (capability call + its ordering constraint) that a method's frozen artifacts contain as
authored structure. Covered instances: 1.0 for both baselines by construction; held-out: what the baseline would have
needed and did not have (e.g. L3: every call exists, the composition does not). Ours: 0.0 by construction (the freeze
audit checks it). Reported once per instance x method in the table beside success, not per run.
**Alternative:** keep the per-run label and report it only as a method-level description in the text.

## 2. Failure taxonomy (§15), one primary category per failed run

1. perception / semantic interpretation (a wrong reading of the scene or an indicator)
2. mission-model coverage / decomposition (the method had no continuation: baselines' escalation on held-out)
3. planner / executive failure (EUROPA no plan, PLEXIL plan error, Ours reasoning loop error or step budget)
4. capability / controller failure after the tier-1 budget (a shared skill failed three times: physical layer)
5. invariant / authority guard (blocked; a guard false positive is reviewed separately)
6. verification failure (effect judged wrongly: false success or false failure)
7. operator / communication (a needed answer never came: denied, unanswered, loss of signal)
8. infrastructure (simulator crash, DDS, farm, model-provider outage)

Assigned from the logs by one engineer with the rule "the first failure on the causal path", checked by a second
reading of the trace; ambiguous cases keep both labels in a note. Stated in limitations (one engineer).

## 3. Exclusion and rerun rules

- Category 8 (infrastructure): fixed, and the run is repeated from the start; never scored. A post-freeze fix that
  changes shared code reruns the affected campaign from the start (execution_plan §13.1).
- Model-provider outage: recorded by the harness as a service outage; a run whose mission could not proceed because
  of it is category 8.
- Category 4 (physical layer): scored as a failure of the run for the main metric (the robot did not complete), and
  reported separately as "success conditioned on no physical-layer failure" (heldout_design §9), for all methods.
- Everything else is scored as is. No run is dropped for any other reason.
- Loss of signal (Earth sets 925 s of mission time after the start, every run; heldout_design §5.3): an escalation
  (a request with no call held for approval) sent while Earth is down, or whose answer Earth's setting holds back, counts
  as `ground_reauthoring_required` -- the mission still needs a new procedure, the HOLD answer just never arrived. An
  authorization request that is not answered in time is unanswered (category 7). Mission time is the simulator clock:
  a model's deliberation runs at the sim/wall ratio (~0.2), so each request's wall-clock send time is reported beside
  its mission time (from the model_io record) as a robustness figure; no rerun.

## 4. Statistics (fixed before the campaign, shown on step 9 rows first)

- Autonomous success per method x level (and per instance: k of n), Wilson 95% intervals; paired by instance.
- The claim is the interaction method x coverage: degradation from covered to held-out per method, shown as the
  success-versus-level curve; with n this small it is reported descriptively with intervals, no significance-driven
  test chosen after seeing data.
- HIR, waiting time, neglect time: medians with bootstrap intervals; interaction level as an ordinal distribution.
- Ours' model variance: every held-out instance three times (heldout_design §14); revisited once, after the first
  held-out variance is seen, and then fixed.
- Scripts: `evaluation/rows.py` -> `evaluation/tables.py` (+ the trace-completeness checker), run unchanged on the
  campaign rows; figure scripts the same way. No hand-edited table.
